sources.entry: Serendipity - Serendipity (s9y) is a highly extensible and customizable PHP blog engine using Smarty templating. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause PHP

summary.one_liner: Serendipity (s9y) is a PHP-powered weblog engine for running a blog, extensible through plugins and themes.
summary.what_it_does: Serendipity provides a blog editor for writing entries, with categories, a media library for uploading images, videos and files into posts, and support for trackbacks and pingbacks. It includes integrated anti-spam measures, a selectable set of themes in the backend, and groups and user management. A plugin management interface lets users add plugins from the backend without manually uploading files. Plugins can add features such as static pages (turning it into a small CMS), extra anti-spam options, tags, and Markdown or Textile markup support. The README describes it as a reliable, secure and extensible framework for both casual and professional blogging.
use_cases: host a small CMS with static pages
manage multiple blog users and groups
add Markdown support to blog posts
how_to_run: On most hosts, Serendipity is already supported; no extra install needed
On a custom server, install PHP >= 8.0, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite, and Apache
Download a release archive and upload the files to your webroot
Visit your URL in a browser to start the installer
See the manual for more details
notable: Plugins can be installed from the backend interface without manual file uploads
Smarty-based templating and a selectable theme collection
Built-in media library for images, videos and other files
Expandable framework that can grow into a small CMS via plugins
Independent, open development team with a path to contributor access
caveats: Requires a PHP, database and web server stack (PHP >= 8.0 plus MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite, and Apache) on custom servers
Static pages, tags and Markdown/Textile depend on third-party plugins rather than core features
